paras: The killing of James Kelly at Whistler, Alabama, was the fatal shooting of a Black man at a colored fair at Whistler, a few miles from Mobile, on the night of August 17, 1880. Kelly was shot by a man described as a creole, Antone Hennenberg, who escaped the next morning. The killing was known outside Alabama through a single Mobile telegraphic dispatch that ran as a one-line crime item in papers from New York to Texas.

According to a dispatch dated at Mobile on August 18, the shooting took place "last night" at Whistler, which the New-York Tribune placed five miles from Mobile and the Knoxville Daily Chronicle seven. Kelly, called "a negro" in the dispatch, was "shot and instantly killed" at a colored fair by Hennenberg, whom every version identified only as "a creole." The reports gave no cause for the shooting and said nothing of a quarrel or of anyone else taking part.

Hennenberg "escaped this morning," the Knoxville version of the dispatch said, and the Wilmington Daily Republican likewise ended its item with the words "Hennemberg escaped." No report of an arrest, an inquest or a trial appears in the coverage.

Papers in Lancaster, Wilmington, Knoxville, New York and Dallas all printed the Mobile dispatch on August 19, usually as a single sentence among accidents, drownings and other killings. The New-York Tribune headed it "An Alabama Murder" in its telegraphic "Crimes and Casualties" column, and the Knoxville Daily Chronicle ran it under "Murder" on August 19 and again, unchanged, on August 20. The Alexandria Gazette rewrote the item, dating the shooting "Tuesday night," and set it under an "Outrages" heading beside a fatal fight among Black excursionists in Delaware.

None of the papers commented on the killing, and the names were garbled in transmission, with the victim printed as "James Keller" in Knoxville and "Joseph Kelly" in Dallas. No Black-press report of the killing was found.

The Mobile dispatch and the Alexandria Gazette placed the shooting on the night of Tuesday, August 17, while the Wilmington Daily Republican, writing on August 19, said it happened "yesterday." The Mobile-datelined version is the closer source, and the Wilmington date appears to follow the date of the dispatch rather than of the shooting.

reader.title: Killing of James Kelly at Whistler, Alabama
bases: Every report describes a single shooting of a Black man by one named man at a colored fair, with no mob, officers, or stated racial motive (A1, A3, A4, A6).

All reports derive from one Mobile telegraphic dispatch of Aug. 18, carried or rewritten by papers in Pennsylvania, Delaware, Tennessee, New York, Texas and Virginia (A1, A2, A3, A4, A6); no local Alabama or independent account was found.

accounts.label: Mobile wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Last night at Whistler, five (or seven) miles from Mobile, a Black man named James Kelly was shot and instantly killed by a creole named Antone Hennenberg at a colored fair; some versions add that the shooter escaped that morning.

framing.detail: Northern and Southern dailies ran the Mobile dispatch as a one-sentence item in telegraphic crime-and-casualty columns, headed 'An Alabama Murder' or 'Murder', with no comment.

The Alexandria Gazette rewrote the item under an 'Outrages' heading next to a fatal fight among Black excursionists in Delaware and an arrest of a Black man at Mobile, without comment on the killing itself.

conflicts.note: The Mobile-datelined dispatches are the closer source; the Wilmington summary appears to have dated the event from the dispatch date.
